title: contract-risk-tiering-and-forecast-adjustment-playbook-2026
author: Daniel Park
body:
Overview

This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standardized approach for: (1) assigning a risk tier to commercial contracts and procurement commitments that materially affect revenue or cash flow, and (2) applying governed forecast adjustments and RevRec flags into the revenue forecasting pipeline (RevRecPipeline). The goal is to ensure consistent, auditable adjustments to forecasts and to reduce manual ad hoc changes during quarter closes or large customer negotiations.

Scope

- Applies to all ARR or committed spend > $25k ARR or one-time deals with > $100k impact.
- Covers direct sales, channel/marketplace deals, managed Dedicated/Private engagements, and supplier commitments that affect COGS.
- Excludes routine small procurement (under $5k) and standard renewals below thresholds.

Owners and stakeholders

- Playbook owner: Finance Contracts & Forecasting (finance-legal).
- Approvers: Head of Finance, VP Sales for customer-side changes > $250k, Legal for non-standard terms.
- Executors: Revenue Operations (RevOps), Contract Operations (ContractsOps), Procurement Ops.
- Observability: FP&A (forecast reconciliation), RevRec team (accounting recognition adjustments).

When to use this playbook

Use this procedure whenever a contract or procurement item meets any of the following triggers:

1. New or amended customer contract with MRR/ARR impact >= $25k.
2. One-time professional services or implementation fees >= $100k.
3. Supplier agreement with committed spend >= $200k or multi-year obligations affecting gross margin.
4. Contract contains non-standard terms (data residency, escrow, extended indemnity, unusual termination penalties).

Contract risk tiering matrix

Assign a risk tier to each qualifying contract using the following scoring. The combined score determines the tier and the forecast action required.

Scoring table (points):

- Counterparty credit: Strong financials (0), Moderate (5), Weak or startup (12)
- Contract duration: 0-12 months (0), 13-24 months (4), 25+ months (8)
- Payment terms: Prepaid/Net0 (0), Net30 (2), Net60 (6), Net90+ or milestone (10)
- Termination provisions: Standard (0), 30–90 day notice (3), Material exit cost/penalty (10)
- Delivery complexity: Standard API/hosted (0), Dedicated/private deployment (6), On-prem air-gapped with integration services (12)
- Legal exceptions: None (0), Minor non-standard clauses (4), Major exceptions/escalations (15)

Tier thresholds (sum of points):

- Tier A (Low risk): 0–9 points -> Forecast treatment: Count full committed ARR, no conservative holdbacks.
- Tier B (Medium risk): 10–19 points -> Forecast treatment: Apply 10% conservative haircut to ARR in near-term quarters and flag for weekly monitoring.
- Tier C (High risk): 20+ points -> Forecast treatment: Exclude from best-case forecast; include in upside bucket only. Require executive sign-off to include in baseline.

Example assignment

A 3-year Dedicated deployment with Net60 payment, customer classified as moderate credit and includes a 6-month implementation milestone with an unusual termination clause: points = duration (8) + payment (6) + delivery (6) + credit (5) + termination (10) = 35 -> Tier C.

Forecast adjustment procedures (RevOps + FP&A)

1. Intake and tagging
   - ContractsOps ingests executed contract into ContractRegistry (internal Confluence link: /contracts/registry) and tags metadata: counterparty, start_date, end_date, ARR, one_time_fees, payment_terms, delivery_type, legal_exceptions.
   - If ARR >= threshold, mark record with field risk_tiering_required = true.

2. Risk scoring
   - ContractsOps runs the scoring worksheet (Google Sheet template: ContractRiskScoring_v2) and saves the signed PDF into the contract record.
   - For deals with ambiguous inputs, escalate to Legal for clause interpretation and to Finance for credit verification.

3. Forecast system update
   - RevOps maps the contract into ForecastSystem (internal tool) as one of: baseline, upside, or excluded.
   - For Tier B: forecast line entry must include a "haircut_percentage" parameter (default 10%).
   - For Tier C: create a separate opportunity line item in ForecastSystem with stage = "Upside - High Risk" and set probability = 15% by default.
   - Adjustments are applied via automation job: 
     - CLI example: billing-cli forecast-adjust --contract-id C-12345 --action apply-haircut --percent 10 --reason "Tier B scoring"

4. RevRec pipeline flags
   - RevRecPipeline must be notified of any material change (> $50k) via the RevRec API.
   - Payload must include: contract_id, risk_tier, haircut_pct, effective_date, fp_owner.
   - Accounting will surface resulting deferred revenue journal entries for review in the next close cycle.

5. Monitoring and re-evaluation
   - Tier B items: RevOps owns weekly monitor with KPIs: signed-amendment rate, days-to-first-invoice, cash-collection delta. Trigger thresholds: if days-to-first-invoice > 60 or collection delta > 20% vs. expected -> escalate to Head of Finance.
   - Tier C items: require bi-weekly review until contract passes 6 months of on-time billing.

Sign-off and exception workflow

- Any attempt to include Tier C revenue into baseline requires written sign-off from: Head of Finance + Sales lead + VP Customer Success. The sign-off must be recorded in the contract record and in the FP&A approval queue.
- Exceptions to tiering decisions: ContractsOps can propose an override with annotated rationale; overrides must include quantitative evidence (credit memo, escrow, bank guarantee) and be approved by Legal + Head of Finance.

Procurement commitments that affect forecasting

- Supplier contracts that create ongoing COGS exposure or multi-year commitments are scored using a complementary supplier risk rubric (supplier credit, termination, volume minimums, geographic restrictions).
- For procurement obligations >= $200k, Procurement Ops creates a forecast liability line and tags FP&A for margin impact assessment.

Configuration and integration checklist

- ContractRegistry: must store structured fields for risk scoring, signed PDF, and link to ForecastSystem.
- ForecastSystem: support fields -> risk_tier, haircut_pct, visibility (baseline/upside/excluded), contract_id.
- RevRecPipeline: accept webhook or API call from RevOps with schema version v2.1.
- Billing system (ChargingService/Stripe): support holdback invoicing and milestone-based billing.

Minimum data fields required on ingestion (table):

| field_name | type | required | example |
| contract_id | string | yes | C-2026-1023 |
| counterparty | string | yes | Acme Analytics, Inc. |
| arr | number | conditional | 120000 |
| one_time_fees | number | no | 150000 |
| payment_terms | string | yes | Net60 |
| delivery_type | string | yes | Dedicated |
| start_date | date | yes | 2026-01-15 |
| end_date | date | yes | 2029-01-14 |
| legal_exceptions | string | conditional | "extended indemnity; data escrow" |

Audit and reporting

- Monthly report: FP&A publishes "Risk-Tier Forecast Impact" deck on the 5th business day. It must include: total ARR in each tier, projected haircut impact by quarter, new Tier C additions, and open sign-off items.
- Quarterly audit: Internal Audit will sample 10 Tier B/C contracts per quarter to ensure scoring and approvals match records.

Training and enablement

- ContractsOps and RevOps must complete the Risk Tiering training module (Workday Learning ID: FT-RT-01) upon hire and annually.
- Playbook walkthroughs are scheduled during QBRs between Finance and Sales Operations.

Appendix: common scenarios and recommended actions

1. Customer requests long payment terms to ramp usage: If Net90 requested, score payment_terms = 10 points -> likely Tier C unless backed by prepayment or bank guarantee. Consider alternate structures: partial prepayment + staged deliveries.

2. Large Marketplace listing with percentage-of-volume payouts: Treat marketplace commitments as revenue sharing; score based on payment lag and guaranteed minima. Notify RevRec to model variable consideration.

3. Rapidly scaling startup customer with strong product traction but weak credit: Consider escrow, card-on-file with holdback, or require a 2-month prepaid deposit before moving from Tier C to Tier B.
